title: The Weekly Energy Fingerprint: What Household Demand Tells Us About the Grid
summary: A household power record reveals recurring demand patterns across years, days, hours and circuits, and where useful flexibility may live.
key_takeaway: Electricity demand is behavioural infrastructure: nobody in this household was trying to be flexible, they were just living their week, and a measurable pattern showed up anyway. Measuring that rhythm well, down to the circuit and the hour, turns ordinary routine into a genuine tool for balancing a cleaner grid. The flexibility was already there; it just needed to be seen.

inline_figures.caption: Daily average active power across the multi-year record shows recurring cycles, exceptional peaks and a changing baseline.
Long-run total demand, sub-metered circuits and the average hourly profile reveal different layers of the same household load.
Average hourly profiles show a sharper weekday morning ramp and a higher, differently timed weekend evening peak.
The hour-by-day heatmap locates recurring morning and evening demand peaks across the week.
